Definition: from G1537 and G2064; to issue (literally or figuratively):--come (forth, out), depart (out of), escape, get out, go (abroad, away, forth, out, thence), proceed (forth), spread abroad.
BiblicalUsage: exérchomai means come (forth, out), depart (out of), escape, get out, go (abroad, away, forth, out, thence), proceed (forth), spread abroad. In Matthew 2:6, the text says "for out of thee shall come a Governor." In Mark 1:25, the text says "and come out of him."
TheologicalSignificance: For me, exérchomai is a reminder that the gospel was never meant to stay where it started — it goes out, because God sends it out. That shapes how I read the passages where it appears: not as filler, but as God's own wording for what He is doing.
RelatedEvents: The Birth of John the Baptist; The Calling of the First Disciples; The Magi Visit Jesus
